highlights.title: What’s new, right on the bridge page
highlights.blurb: A pill tells you when a new release is out. Open it to see every change, grouped like the release notes, and update in one click.
highlights.alt: The Update available pill opens the What’s new drawer: the update card on top, then each release’s changes, with betas shown after the toggle.

highlights.title: Learn REAPER while the agent works
highlights.blurb: Type /teach and every change comes with what it did and why, the REAPER concept behind it, how to do it by hand, and the before and after, with a link to the change on the bridge page.
highlights.alt: One change fans out to four answers: what it did and why, the REAPER concept, how to do it by hand, before and after with undo.

highlights.title: Ask for a plugin and get one
highlights.blurb: Describe the effect you want and /make-plugin writes it as a JSFX plugin with real knobs and an Advanced drawer, loads it on your track and checks it. It keeps working without the agent.
highlights.alt: A generated plugin, Mutate Verb, shows four knobs, then its Advanced drawer slides up with six more.

highlights.title: Install the REAPER side with ReaPack
highlights.blurb: Add the reaper-mcp repository to ReaPack to install the bridge scripts, the meters and the status page. ReaPack then offers updates like any other package.
highlights.alt: The reaper-mcp repository in ReaPack flows into REAPER: bridge scripts, meters and the status page.

highlights.title: Doubles that land on the guide vocal
highlights.blurb: Ask to tighten a double and the agent moves its hits onto the lead with stretch markers, then checks pitch, tone and attacks. A backing vocal 37 ms late on average lined up in one go. Needs the sidecar.
highlights.tryIt: Ask: align the doubles to the lead vocal
highlights.alt: In REAPER, a quiet backing vocal under the lead gets stretch markers at each phrase, then a check reports pitch, tone and attacks unchanged.
